_readme: SEED ONLY. Applied once, when the sector table is empty — a fresh install must not be a
blank product. After that the table is the source of truth and this file is history: the
platform console edits sectors at RUNTIME (/api/v1/platform/sectors), with no rebuild and no
restart. Re-applying this on every boot would silently undo an operator's edits, which is the
worst kind of bug — the console appears to work, and the change is gone by morning.
FIVE SECTORS. Three were chosen for us: tyres, car wash, women's salon. The other two are:
auto_repair — the largest vehicle market by spend, and the one with the longest, most
valuable service cycles. If retention works anywhere, it works here.
barber      — the highest-FREQUENCY sector in the set, at roughly three weeks. Frequency is
what makes a retention product visible: a customer who returns monthly
produces a measurable result in weeks, not a year.
Between them the five span both asset models (vehicle and none) and cycles from two weeks to
two years, which is the range the reminder engine has to survive.
`cycle_days` is what reminders schedules from. 0 means NO natural cycle — a puncture repair,
a one-off makeup booking — and generates no reminder. Explicitly a value rather than a missing
one: defaulting it to 30 would schedule a reminder for a puncture and teach a customer that
No prices. They vary by city, by shop and by the day; shipping a number ships a wrong one to
almost everybody, and a wrong price on a screen is worse than a blank one.

plate.label: رقم اللوحة
plate.help: المركبة هي الأصل الوحيد في المنتج (§13.2). واللوحة لا تُفرض فرادتها: تُكتب بيد مستعجلة، ورفض المكرر يمنع زيارة حقيقية حمايةً لقيدٍ لم يطلبه أحد.

meter.label: قراءة العداد
meter.help: اختياري دائماً. إلزامه يوقف التسجيل حين لا يقدر العامل على قراءته — والزيارة أهم من الرقم.
